title: Self-heal stamp-clear silently no-ops once the batched send queue runs longer than the new 10-minute freshness window
evidence:
UPDATE inbound_email
SET second_reminder_sent_at = NULL
WHERE vacancy_id = $1
  AND lower(sender_email) = lower($2)
  AND second_reminder_sent_at > now() - interval '10 minutes'
--- and clear_reminder_for_sender.sql: "  AND reminder_sent_at > now() - interval '10 minutes'"
--- and inbound_handler.gleam send_batched: "let batches = list.sized_chunk(emails, 5)" / "True -> process.sleep(1100)" / "case process.receive(subject, 12_000)"
--- and email_client.gleam: "let config = httpc.configure() |> httpc.timeout(10_000)"
--- and send_reminders_background runs stage 2 only after stage 1 fully drains: "send_batched(stage1_recipients, ...) |> list.each(...)" then "send_batched(stage2_recipients, ...)"
detail: The window's premise (stamps are seconds old at clear time) breaks at scale: ~11s/batch of 5 means the combined stage-1+stage-2 queue exceeds 600s at ≈270 recipients (Daft inbound is uncapped). A send failing past that point clears nothing (stamps older than 10 min, `let _ =` swallows it), leaving the enquirer stamped-but-never-sent: stage-1 victims lose remindability and become stage-2 eligible in 2 days; stage-2 victims are permanently blocked (`last_stage2_at > last_stage1_at`).
recommended_fix: Widen the clear window past worst-case queue runtime (e.g. 1 hour) or scope it to the attempt (stamp a batch/attempt id and clear on that), and log when the clear updates zero rows.
